name: MonarchCallStatsPanel
title: CallStatsPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchDescriptionList (Inline) and MonarchStatusBadge per person; presented by the app in MonarchBottomSheet
summary: The data a call has used and each person's round trip, packet loss and connection grade.
whenToUse: In a call's "Connection" sheet or pane, opened from the call controls, when people need to see why audio or video is poor.
whenNotToUse: For a single indicator of call quality in the call view, use a MonarchStatusBadge or MonarchAudioLevelMeter; for analytics over many calls, a chart or a table.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCallStatsPanel(usage: MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage, peers: List<MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, lowData: Boolean = false, footnote: String? = null, labels: MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels = MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels())
class MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage(sentBytes: Long, receivedBytes: Long, upBitsPerSecond: Double? = null, downBitsPerSecond: Double? = null)

class MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id: String, name: String, roundTripMilliseconds: Double? = null, inboundLossPercent: Double? = null, outboundLossPercent: Double? = null, quality: MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.Unknown)
enum class MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality { Good, Fair, Poor, Unknown }

class MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels(dataUsed: String? = null, usageSummary: ((total: String, up: String, down: String) -> String)? = null, lowData: String? = null, connections: String? = null, roundTrip: String? = null, loss: String? = null, noPeers: String? = null, notMeasured: String? = null, qualityNames: Map<MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: usage
options.description: Bytes sent and received, and the current upload and download rates in bits per second.

options.name: peers
options.description: One entry per remote person: name, round trip in milliseconds, inbound and outbound loss in percent, and a grade.

options.name: lowData
options.description: Adds the note "Low data mode is on: audio only.".

options.name: footnote
options.description: A closing note, such as how media is routed or protected. App copy: Monarch does not know how the app connects calls.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the heading, the usage line, the low data note, the list name, Round trip, Loss, the no-peers text, "Not measured yet" and the grade names.

states.name: default
states.description: The heading and the usage line, then one block per person: the name with a grade badge, then Round trip and Loss rows.

states.name: low data
states.description: A muted note under the usage line.

states.name: not measured
states.description: A missing number shows a dash; an unknown grade is a neutral badge "Not measured yet".

states.name: no peers
states.description: "No one else is connected yet." instead of the people.

appearance: The heading is subheading text; the usage line, notes and footnote muted caption text; names body strong text. Grades are small subtle status badges: Good in the success tone, Fair in the warning tone, Poor in the danger tone, Unknown neutral. Rows are an inline description list. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with a column per number and signal bars for the grade; on a phone a four-column table does not fit at large text sizes, so, as on iOS, each person is a block with description list rows and the grade is a MonarchStatusBadge. The parity map named LazyColumn rows in a MonarchBottomSheet: the panel is the sheet's content, not the sheet, because the sheet's state, detents and dismissal belong to the app (see the example and the catalogue page); it is a Column so it also fits a pane or a scrolling sheet. Bytes use powers of 1,024 and rates powers of 1,000, written in the current locale with halves rounded up, as the web's formatCallBytes and formatCallRate do; those helpers are not public API. Loss uses the locale's percent format. iOS uses the same names; isLowData is lowData in Kotlin style.
accessibility: "Data used this call" is a heading; the usage line is plain text.
The people are a traversal group named "Connection to each person".
Each person is one element read as the name, the round trip, the loss and the grade, such as "Alex Chen, Round trip 186 ms, Loss 3.4%, Unstable connection".
A number that was not measured is read as "Not measured yet", not as the dash shown.
The grade is a badge with its name, so it is not told by color alone.
Text wraps and scales with the font size; long names wrap.
edgeCases: Loss shows the worse of the two directions; a direction that is missing or not finite is ignored.
Negative or non-finite rates count as 0 bps; negative byte counts as 0.
The round trip is rounded to whole milliseconds; loss has one decimal.
Rates of 10 Mbps and more have no decimal.
The panel holds no timer: pass new numbers as statistics arrive, every second or two.

examples.title: During a group call
examples.template:
MonarchCallStatsPanel(
    usage = MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage(
        sentBytes = {{usage.sentBytes}},
        receivedBytes = {{usage.receivedBytes}},
        upBitsPerSecond = {{usage.upBps|double}},
        downBitsPerSecond = {{usage.downBps|double}},
    ),
    peers = listOf(
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = {{peers.0.id}}, name = {{peers.0.name}}, roundTripMilliseconds = {{peers.0.rttMs|double}}, inboundLossPercent = {{peers.0.inboundLossPct|double}}, outboundLossPercent = {{peers.0.outboundLossPct|double}}, quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.{{peers.0.quality|pascal}}),
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = {{peers.1.id}}, name = {{peers.1.name}}, roundTripMilliseconds = {{peers.1.rttMs|double}}, inboundLossPercent = {{peers.1.inboundLossPct|double}}, outboundLossPercent = {{peers.1.outboundLossPct|double}}, quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.{{peers.1.quality|pascal}}),
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = {{peers.2.id}}, name = {{peers.2.name}}, quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.{{peers.2.quality|pascal}}),
    ),
    footnote = {{footnote}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchCallStatsPanel(
    usage = MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage(
        sentBytes = 6_200_000,
        receivedBytes = 9_400_000,
        upBitsPerSecond = 420_000.0,
        downBitsPerSecond = 1_250_000.0,
    ),
    peers = listOf(
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = "a", name = "Robin Park", roundTripMilliseconds = 38.0, inboundLossPercent = 0.2, outboundLossPercent = 0.1, quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.Good),
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = "b", name = "Alex Chen", roundTripMilliseconds = 186.0, inboundLossPercent = 3.4, outboundLossPercent = 1.2, quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.Fair),
        MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer(id = "c", name = "Jordan Diaz", quality = MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality.Unknown),
    ),
    footnote = "Example footnote: say here how your product routes and protects call media.",
)

examples.title: Shown in a bottom sheet from the call controls
examples.setup:
var showStats by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
val usage = MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage(sentBytes = 120_000, receivedBytes = 80_000)
